title: Expansion microscopy-based imaging of nuclear structures in cultured cells
protocol: Seed cells on coverslips at 30-50% confluency.
Maintain U2OS cells in DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1× penicillin/streptomycin.
Passage cells every 2-3 days according to standard protocol.
Incubate transfected solution on the dish for 18-20 hours at 37°C after transfection.
Remove media from cells.
Rinse cells twice with 5 mL of warm PBS.
Add 5 mL of warm, freshly-prepared PFA Fixation Solution (4% PFA in PBS) to the dish.
Let sit at 20°C-22°C for 10 minutes.
Remove fixation buffer.
Rinse cells twice with 5 mL of PBS.
Remove PBS and add 5 mL of Permeabilization Solution (1% Triton X-100 in PBS).
Let sit at 20°C–22°C for 10 min.
Rinse cells 2× with 5 mL of PBS.
Transfer coverslips to a Humidified Chamber using fine forceps.
Touch each coverslip carefully against a Kimwipe to remove excess liquid before placing cell side-up on the parafilm.
Pipette 50–100 μL freshly-prepared Blocking Buffer (PBS containing 1% goat serum and 0.1% Tween-20) on top of the cells, ensuring that the entire surface of the coverslip is covered.
Place lid on box and let sit at 20°C–22°C for 10 min.
Clear primary and secondary antibody dilutions in Blocking Buffer by centrifuging at full speed (~21,000 × g) in a refrigerated microcentrifuge for 10 min to pellet any aggregates and store on ice.
Pick up each coverslip and gently touch the edge to a Kimwipe to drain off excess blocking buffer.
Pipette 50–100 μL of primary antibody solution (prepared in Blocking Buffer) on top, ensuring that the entire surface is covered.
Place lid on box and leave for 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Use forceps to transfer each coverslip to a well in a 6-well plate.
Rinse the coverslip with 2 mL PBS for 3 × 5 min.
Remove the coverslip from the well using forceps, touch the edge to Kimwipe to drain off excess PBS.
Place the cell side-up on parafilm inside a humidified chamber.
Gently pipette 50–100 μL of secondary antibody solution (prepared in Blocking Buffer) onto the coverslip, ensuring it is fully covered.
Cover the box and leave for 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Transfer coverslips back to the 6-well plate.
Repeat PBS wash steps as before.
Use species-specific Alexa Fluor® Plus 488 or 555-conjugated secondary antibodies at a concentration of 1:250 dilution (which is 8 μg/mL) for staining endogenous proteins.
If required, use CF633-conjugated secondary antibodies with GFP-tagged proteins.
Use a chicken anti-GFP polyclonal primary antibody at a 1:500 dilution.
Use an Alexa Fluor® 488-conjugated donkey anti-chicken IgY secondary antibody at a 1:500 dilution for amplifying the signal of GFP-tagged proteins.
Mix rat anti-RFP monoclonal primary antibody at a 1:500 dilution with the sample.
Mix Alexa Fluor® Plus 555-conjugated goat anti-rat IgG secondary antibody at a 1:500 dilution with the sample.
Prepare Anchoring Reagent Stock by mixing 10 mg/mL Acryloyl-X in anhydrous DMSO.
Dilute Anchoring Reagent Stock to 0.1 mg/mL in PBS pH7.4 to create the Anchoring Solution.
Drain excess PBS from coverslips.
Place cell side-up on the parafilm in the humidified chamber.
Pipette an 80 μL drop of Anchoring Solution on top of the coverslips.
Ensure that the entire surface is covered with the Anchoring Solution.
Place lid on humidified chamber and incubate for 18–20 hours at 20°C–22°C.
Transfer coverslips back to a 6-well plate.
Wash coverslips 3 times, each for 5 minutes, with PBS.
Weigh out 1.335 g of DMAA and place in a 50 mL conical bottom tube.
Weigh out 0.32 g of Sodium Acrylate, add to the tube, and vortex.
Weigh out 2.85 g of ddH2O, add to the tube, and vortex.
Purge the O2 in the Gelation Solution by bubbling with N2 for 40 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Weigh out 0.036 g KPS and place it in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 1 mL of ddH2O to the KPS and vortex for 1–2 min immediately before use.
Transfer 2.7 mL of purged Gelation Solution to a 15 mL conical bottom tube.
Add 0.3 mL of prepared KPS solution to the gelation solution in the 15 mL tube.
Quickly vortex the mixture for 1-3 seconds after adding KPS.
Purge the O2 in the Gelation Solution by bubbling with N2 for 15 min on ice.
Place a glass slide on a sheet of paper towel as the base of the chamber.
Place 2 blank coverslips (18 × 18 mm, No 1.5) on the slide, a coverslip-width apart, securing each with a drop of water.
Pick up one of the stained/anchored coverslips and touch it carefully against a Kimwipe to remove excess liquid.
Place the cell-side up between the 2 blank coverslips on the slide, moving them inwards to secure tightly.
Carefully place another blank coverslip (18 × 18 mm, No 1.5) on the left side of the cell-containing coverslip, securing it with a drop of water and allowing it to overlap the cells by ~3 mm.
Repeat placing the blank coverslip on the right side to secure the cell-containing coverslip tightly.
Transfer 500 μL of Gelation Solution to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 2 μL of TEMED to the Gelation Solution and vortex for 1–3 seconds.
Pipette 75 μL of the mixture on top of the cell-containing coverslip.
Carefully lower a 22 × 22 mm, No 2 coverslip on top, pushing gently to force out any air bubbles.
Allow gels to polymerize for 2–3 hours by incubating Gelation Chambers at 20°C–22°C in a Humidified Chamber.
Use fine forceps to gently pry up the top coverslip of the Gelation Chamber.
Slide a scalpel blade lengthwise under the edge of the coverslip and gently lever it upwards to avoid breakage.
Transfer the coverslip with attached gel to a 35 mm dish, with the gel facing up.
If the gel remains attached to the original coverslip, carefully pry that coverslip off the slide and transfer it to the 35 mm dish with the gel facing up.
Place the coverslip gel side-up in a 35 mm dish after removing it from the Gelation Chamber.
Transfer the coverslip containing the attached gel to a 35 mm dish if necessary.
Add digestion buffer to the dish containing the gel and secure the lid with parafilm to prevent evaporation.
Place the sealed dish in a humidified chamber containing a damp tissue and transfer it to a water bath set at 50°C.
Close the lid of the dish and leave for 18-20 hours.
Transfer the digested gel to a 10 cm Petri dish after digestion.
Add ddH2O with Hoechst dye to start expansion/DNA staining in the Petri dish.
Change ddH2O at least three times over approximately one hour.
Prepare Digestion Buffer with 50 mM Tris, 800 mM guanidine HCl, 1 mM EDTA, and 0.5% Triton X-100 in ddH2O at pH 8.0.
Add Proteinase K to the Digestion Buffer at a concentration of 8 U/mL.
Add 2 mL of Digestion Solution to each 35 mm dish containing a gel.
Seal the lid to the dish with a strip of parafilm.
Place the dishes in a humidified chamber for an incubation period of 18–20 hours at 50°C.
Remove gel from Digestion Solution by inverting the 35 mm dish onto a 100 mm dish.
Prepare sufficient Expansion/Staining Buffer by mixing 2 μL of 25 mg/mL Hoechst 33342 in 30 mL ddH2O.
Add the Expansion/Staining Buffer to the 100 mm dish with the gel and incubate for 20 min at 20°C–22°C.
Carefully remove the Expansion/Staining Buffer from the dish and replace with ddH2O.
Continue to incubate at 20°C–22°C for 30–40 min, changing water at least three times until no further expansion is observed.
Remove all ddH2O from the 100 mm dish before proceeding.
Design the Gel Cutter using Freecad, providing .FCStd and .stl files as Data S1.
Print the Gel Cutter for 4 hours using a fine tip nozzle.
Excise segments with internal dimensions matching those of an ibidi 8-well μ-Slide using the custom Gel Cutter.
Press the gel cutter firmly down on the gel until it touches the bottom of the plate.
Use a scalpel to slice from the cutter to the edge of the gel so that it can be moved carefully to a clear section of the dish for removal.
If the segment remains in the cutter when it is lifted from the dish, use the pusher to eject it.
Transfer the gel segment carefully using a bent metal spatula.
Move the excised gel segment to an ibidi μ-Slide 8 Well Chambered Coverslip.
Remove any excess liquid from the well to minimize movement of the gel segment during imaging.
Lower the Gel Cutter onto the expanded gel and push down firmly until it touches the bottom of the dish.
Use a scalpel blade to cut from the Gel Cutter to the edge of the gel so that the segment can be removed.
If the segment remains in the cutter, gently push out using the 3D-printed Gel Pusher.
Slide a bent metal spatula blade under the gel segment and lift it out of the dish.
Lower the gel segment into a well of the ibidi 8-well μ-Slide.
Adjust so that it is aligned and fills the well.
Repeat for a second well, but this time invert the gel segment.
Using the microscope system of your choice, identify which well has the gel segment in the correct orientation.
If you cannot bring the Hoechst-stained nuclei into focus using a high resolution/short working distance objective, the gel is upside-down.
Imaging Timing: [varies]
Set up imaging using a standard widefield system.
Image expansion gels with a restoration deconvolution system.
Use a confocal system with a higher resolution imaging mode for imaging.
Ensure the orientation of the gel is cell-side down when using high resolution objectives.
Image the gels in either orientation using a Zeiss AxioObserver D1 widefield system with a 20×/0.8 NA air objective.
Bring embedded cells into focus on a DeltaVision Core restoration deconvolution system using a 60×/1.4 NA oil objective oriented toward the bottom of the chambered slide.
Observe small nuclear foci in expansion gels to achieve higher resolution detail.
Acquire high resolution images using a Zeiss LSM880 AxioObserver Z1 confocal laser scanning microscope equipped with a 63×/1.4 NA Plan-Apochromat oil immersion objective in Airyscan mode.
Set the pixel size of the multichannel Z-stack to 0.04 μm x 0.04 μm x 0.14 μm.
Set the dwell time per pixel to 1.21 μs with no averaging.
Use 405 nm, 488 nm and 561 nm lasers at 2% power for imaging.
Process images by background subtraction to ease rendering steps.
Create a 3D surface rendering for each channel using Imaris 9.6.0 (Bitplane).
Set smoothing of 2× the pixel size (0.08 μm) and threshold for background subtraction of the diameter of the smallest nucSF (~0.35 μm in this case).
Apply a surface filter to keep only the more specific regions of the image.
Confirm that the histone modification signal spreads out and around the centers of nuclear stress foci marked by accumulations of GFP-RepoMan.
Excise a smaller segment of the gel using a scalpel blade when testing the protocol for the first time or whenever deformations or cracks are observed.
Place the excised gel segment in an imaging chamber (e.g., a 35 mm glass-bottom dish) for expansion and direct comparison before and after expansion.
